metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Multivariate normality is often assumed in statistical procedures, but it is less often tested. In LW Chapter 11 we briefly discussed two approaches for testing univariate normality, one graphical and the other based on deviations of observed skewness and/or kurtosis from Gaussian expectations. As we now demonstrate, both of these approaches can be extended to testing for multivariate normality. Additional methods are reviewed by Malkovich and Afifi (1973), Gnanadesikan (1977), Cox and Small (1978), Seber (1984), Looney (1995), and Henze (2002).
